Spot premium quotations for imported cathode remained flat and subdued over the past two weeks as the significant negative arbitrage between the SHFE and the LME remained unchanged. Traders reported that the latest spot premium quotations for imported cathode remained in the US$30-70/t range, with major traders offering cathode at around $50/t. Spot premium quotations for SXEW cathode were quoted at between US$30/t and $50/t. There were very few deals closed given the persisting RMB3000-4000/t import loss. Some market insiders believe that the current SHFE/LME arbitrage, low spot premiums and © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **March 2012** www.crugroup.com the surge in bonded stocks mirror the situation in H1 2011. Whether the SHFE/LME arbitrage window will re-open in May 2012, as was the case in H1 2011, is a key concern amongst many market insiders. We are inclined to believe it will not, given the high inventory levels of refined copper and semis products, combined with lacklustre demand prospects. We were told by market participants that cathode inventories in bonded warehouses currently amount to 550,000-600,000t, which is a rise of around 115,000t over the past two weeks. We attribute this to traders attempting to avoid incurring losses through not selling imported metal on the spot market at the currently low prices. We expect inventories of bonded materials to continue to increase in the short term and bring downward pressure on copper prices. # February surge in copper imports not driven by demand ## **Chinese importsSHFE inventory heads higher (000t)of unwrought and semis-finished copper products** '000t

According to preliminary customs data, China’s unwrought copper and copper semis imports surged to 484,570t in February, up 17.1% m-o-m. We estimate that refined copper accounts for around 400,000t. This contradicts most market insiders’ prior expectations. We estimate that the apparent consumption of refined copper in the first two months of this year was 1,6Mt, up 45.9% y-o-y, with refined copper production reaching 870,000t, up 6.9% y-o-y based on NBS data

. The strong apparent consumption coincides with weak demand and has led to the high levels of cathode inventory. We believe that the increase in refined copper imports was not driven by strong demand; instead, it can be attributed to two main factors. Firstly, some spot shipments booked in December have been delayed to February due to the January holiday, and secondly, we have recently witnessed robust imports of copper as collateral. We believe that real consumption was subdued as we have reiterated in recent reports. Moreover, the recent increase in cathode imports is reflected in a rise in both SHFE and non-reported inventory. The SHFE cathode inventory increased by 131,562t compared to the end of 2011. Shanghai bonded stocks increased by 325,000t over the same period. At the same time, semis and refined copper producers’ cathode stocks are estimated to have risen by around 50,000t at the end of February compared to the end 2011. Overall, the above stock changes amount to a just over 500,000t rise in cathode inventories, which we expect will put supply side pressure on prices in the short term. At the same time, it will keep the negative SHFE/LME arbitrage from narrowing. We have heard reports that cathode imports as collateral declined recently due to the moderate credit easing and the effects of the negative arbitrage. Although it is difficult to track the volume of cathode imports for financing, we believe that it will probably remain strong in March. In addition, some market insiders anticipate that cathode exports may rise to around 30,000t in March, as smelters engage in the copper concentrate tolling business. On balance, we expect net imports to fall in March, as the arbitrage © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 5 **March 2012** www.crugroup.com has been significantly negative since 10th January. China’s power industry investment from 2016 to 2020 is forecast to reach RMB7.1 trillion, up 16.4% compared to 2011-2015, including a power generation investment of RMB3.6 trillion and a power grid investment of RMB3.5 trillion. We believe that the above investments will boost copper consumption in the long term. # Copper prices trade sideways The LME 3-month copper price ranged between $8,300/t and 8,500/t over the past two weeks. Subdued Chinese demand and gloomy demand prospects in the coming months had a negative effect on copper prices. However, the ongoing supply disruptions and the high level of the LME copper cancelled warrants have prevented the copper price from declining. Similarly, the SHFE 3-month copper prices fluctuated between RMB59,470-61,190/t over the past two weeks. The National People’s Congress and Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference ended this week. China’s Premier Wen Jiabao announced that the GDP target was cut to 7.5% this year, which indicates that the government will not push GDP growth as strongly as before. The economy should therefore return to reasonable and sustainable growth. We believe that the impact on the copper market will be negative, mainly due to market sentiment. In addition, he announced that the regulation on real estate will not relax and house prices are a long way away from reaching a reasonable level, meaning that the severe macro control on the property market will continue. This will constrain copper consumption growth in property and related industries (e.g. household appliances). However, in positive news, there is increased scope for monetary policy to ease as inflation has declined, which will support demand in the future. Market insiders expect monetary easing to take place in H2 2012. In terms of our short term copper price outlook, we forecast that the SHFE 3-month copper price will range between RMB59,000/t and RMB61,000/t in the next two weeks. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 4
